Sophie (Support): forwarding a CX ticket from AcmeCorp — they say invoice INV-2026-0894 (EUR) doesn't reconcile with the usage dashboard. customer sees three line items but totals differ by ~0.03 EUR. attached snippet below.

Sophie (Support): ```
Invoice: INV-2026-0894
currency: EUR
lines: [ {desc: 'tokens', net: 10.12, vat: 1.52, gross: 11.64}, {desc: 'priority-surcharge', net: 0.50, vat: 0.08, gross: 0.58}, {desc: 'rounding_adj', net: -0.01, vat: 0.01, gross: 0.00} ]
total_gross: 12.22
dashboard_total_gross: 12.25
```

Mike (Billing): thanks. Do we know if the customer was billed in EUR or converted from USD? any per-request exchange rates applied? also need raw token counts (per-request) for the day.

Sophie (Support): they were on EUR-priced plan, no conversion on invoice. sent sample usage export (s3 link). customer also attached a screenshot showing dashboard sum = 12.25.

Julie (Eng-Platform): quick hypothesis: aggregator does per-request rounding to 2 decimals before summing then applies VAT proration across lines. if you round at request level, small micro-euro truncation accumulates. snippet of current logic: ```python
def add_request(amount_eur):
    rounded = round(amount_eur, 2)
    line_totals.append(rounded)
    return sum(line_totals)```
This will differ from summing raw amounts and rounding once at invoice. :thinking_face:

Kevin (Eng-ML): also saw a token-count mismatch earlier — dashboard uses tokenizer v1 that counts newlines differently than billing pipeline's tokenizer which normalizes whitespace. that changes billed tokens slightly. repro: `python -c "from tokenizer_v1 import t; print(len(t.encode('Hello\nWorld')))"` vs billing's `tokenizer.normalize(...)`.

Lenka (Finance Ops): VAT handling matters here. we prorate VAT across lines after conversion/rounding. edge-case: negative rounding_adj line is produced when per-line rounding overshoots; invoice formatting hides microcent adjustment in net but shows 0.00 gross which confuses customers. we should surface a dedicated "rounding adjustment" line with explicit sign.

Mike (Billing): agreed. propose short-term mitigation: 1) update invoice renderer to always include explicit rounding_adjustment as visible line; 2) change aggregation to sum raw smallest-units (micro-euro cents) then round once at invoice level; 3) coordinate with Eng to align tokenizer versions. I'll open a billing patch and schedule a deploy to staging.

Julie (Eng-Platform): PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/986 — moves rounding to the final step and emits rounding_adjustment line. staging tests added. expecting small diff in existing invoices for ~0.01-0.05 EUR per invoice.

Kevin (Eng-ML): I'll add a migration in dashboard exporter to use billing tokenizer (match exact billing pipeline) so dashboards show same token counts. small flag `?tokenizer=billing` added to usage export for now.

Lenka (Finance Ops): can we also add a quick script to backfill last 30 days invoice visible rounding line for affected customers? customers want explanation, not just numbers. I'll prepare communication template.
